response.sql: WITH m AS (SELECT o.mktnote AS pair, f.feerate - f.rebrate AS net FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = f.orderslink), g AS (SELECT pair, AVG(net) AS avg_net FROM m GROUP BY pair), b AS (SELECT AVG(net) AS bench FROM m) SELECT AVG(g.avg_net) AS avg_of_pair_avg_net_rate, AVG(g.avg_net - b.bench) AS avg_excess_over_benchmark FROM g CROSS JOIN b WHERE g.avg_net > b.bench

assumptions.assumption: A fee's net rate is NULL when either feerate or rebrate is NULL, so that fee record is skipped in the averages. The benchmark still counts each non-missing fee record equally.
orders.recordvault is unique, so the join does not duplicate fee records.
Pairs whose average net rate is NULL (all net rates missing) are never kept, because NULL > benchmark is not true.
